correctness.rationale: For complex Gaussian measure, moments reduce the squared ratio to \((E_4-|a|^4)/(E_4-E_2^2)\). Monotonicity in \(E_4\) forces the optimal coefficient phase. Cases with \(a=0\), \(b=0\), or \(c=0\) have ratio at most 2. On \(F=x+z-yz^2\) the exact quotient \(N/D\) has a unique x-maximizer for each y>0. The polynomial resultant of the x- and y-stationary equations has a single admissible positive root, and the profile tends to 2 at both ends, giving the unique global maximizer. Gaussian orthogonality, all derivative identities and resultant were verified symbolically, and independent quadrature tests passed; the proof does not infer infinite sharpness from finite samples.

The May 2026 source proves a different modulus phase-retrieval estimate and an orthogonal linear coercivity estimate. An exact algebraic three-mode sharp constant with optimizer classification is not a stated or logically immediate corollary of either. No equivalent or dominating result was identified in performed searches; unindexed prior calculations remain possible.
residual_risks: A prior article or unindexed computation may independently contain the same algebraic constant or a stronger moment inequality.

value.rationale: The sector \(\operatorname{span}\{1,z,z^2\}\) is the canonical first nonlinear Hermite truncation; exact \(C_2\) identifies the first departure from affine square-coercivity \(C=\sqrt2\) and forces nontrivial negative phase alignment. The coefficient \(C_2\) is a sharp obstruction for the unrestricted universal inequality of Bortolotto–Ramos, and its unique optimizer is a natural reproducibility benchmark. The result is restricted but not an arbitrary isolated numerical slice.
